newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares forge ahead, defy warnings.
newsitem.headline: German shares forge ahead, defy warnings.

text.p: German shares look set to continue to pursue a relentlessly upward course as long as the dollar underscores their rally, but dealers were uncertain late on Monday how long the U.S. currency's support can last.
Dealers were variously delighted or taken aback by the DAX's steady climb but agreed that there appeared to be no factors about to brake it.

"We have broken through so much resistance at this point that the technicals don't seem to matter anymore," said one dealer. "There doesn't seem to be any reason to buy Bunds and loads of reasons to buy equity."
The 30-share IBIS DAX was up 61 points, or 1.5 percent, at 4,135.30 points at 1402 GMT, far beyond the 4,110-point resistance level many dealers expected the DAX to baulk at earlier in the day.
September DTB DAX futures were up 72 points at 4,165 points.
Export shares were the logical winners of the day.
The dollar held firm at six-year highs against the mark through the day, climbing to new highs of more than 1.79 marks, while sterling also surged to pass above three marks.
However the insurance sector also outperformed.

Muenchener Rueckversicherungs AG was up 218 marks, or 3.6 percent, at 6,353.70 marks as it extended gains from Friday, when it reported better than expected earnings per share of 150 marks for the 1996/1997 business year.

Various banks cautioned against exaggerated rallies on the DAX, with Trinkaus & Burkhardt drawing attention to the fact that Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer had expressed some concern about asset inflation last week.
DG Bank said the DAX could hit a high of 4,160 points this week before technical factors force a consolidation.
